Chapter 10: Cultivating a Wider Awareness.
You know, awareness is a lot like a muscle—the more you use it, the stronger it gets.
Most of us start out with a pretty narrow focus, just because that’s what we’re used to. But, what if you could actually train yourself to open up your field of attention? To really notice more of what’s going on around you—and inside you?
Picture this: someone who’s always been on the shy side, hanging back at parties or group events. Then, one evening, they decide to do something different. They step up, start a conversation with someone new. At first, it’s a bit awkward—maybe even uncomfortable. But after a few moments, they find something in common, and suddenly, the world feels a little bigger, a bit more inviting.
That’s the kind of shift this chapter is all about. The author shares a few simple ways to start expanding your awareness. It could be as easy as pausing for a moment to listen to the sounds in the room, or tuning in to the sensations in your body. Maybe it’s just noticing the emotions that drift through your mind. These aren’t tricks to reach some special state, or to turn you into someone you’re not. They’re about waking up—to everything that’s already here.
Here’s something most people miss: we tend to think our attention is set in stone, that we’re either locked-in or completely distracted. But it’s actually much more flexible than that. With a little intention and some practice, you can shift that spotlight. You can take in more of the world—and respond to it with greater wisdom.
The stories in this chapter really bring it to life. Imagine a parent who starts noticing those subtle cues from their child—a glance, a sigh, a quiet moment—and is able to meet needs that were never spoken out loud. Or a leader who picks up on the mood of a team, and chooses just the right moment to step in and encourage. Even a friend who simply senses when to reach out, just because they’re paying attention.
Those small moments of expanded awareness? They make a difference. They ripple out, shaping lives in ways you might not even see right away.
The real challenge is to keep practicing—to keep widening that lens. Because the world is so much bigger than we sometimes remember. And there’s always more to see.
